name: Search-Heavy Knowledge Base
tagline: A support knowledge base where almost every request is a search.
realWorld: An operations knowledge base fronted by a search box: readers arrive with a query rather than a URL, type into an autocomplete on the way, and open one or two articles. Reads of a single record are the minority.

traffic.desc: the ordinary query: full text over title and body, ranked, first page
the same query with snippets, which adds two ts_headline calls per row
autocomplete as the reader types: a prefix LIKE on the title, several per query typed
faceted counts, which run one extra grouped query per facet field
the third page of results, where the count is repeated and the offset is skipped
a search with no query text, which is a browse ordered by last update and takes no ranking
opening one article, which is the content router rather than search
the slug lookup a result link turns into, because there is no get-by-slug route
browsing a category, filtered on the foreign key because search cannot filter a relation

_note: Load-test manifest for this example. The content types are NOT listed here: perf/export-profiles.mjs reads them from the running engine so they cannot drift from the app. This file declares only what the app itself does not: benchmark-scale seed volumes, the arrival rate, the thresholds, and the weighted request mix. The mix is search-heavy on purpose, because every other profile exercises the content router and treats search as a rounding error. Two absences are deliberate. Every search entry is on the admin router, because there is no public search route and no arrangement in which a browser calls one. And no entry posts to /api/admin/search/analytics/log, even though a real deployment writes one per search, because the engine records nothing itself and the manifest has no vocabulary for a request body. A driver that gains one should add that write at roughly the weight of search-term.
